correctness.rationale: For odd p, q=p^e, N=q+1, n|N with n,r=N/n>=2, the integral plane curve Y^N=X^(2n)Z^(N-2n)+X^n Z^(N-n) has n local branches over the affine origin contributing polar base degree N(n-1). At r>2 the ng branches at infinity (g=gcd(r,2)) yield B_inf=N(N-2n-1), raised by 2n exactly if p|(r-2); r=2 has smooth infinity. The polar linear series degree is 2n^2 or N(n+1) minus the exceptional 2n. Crucially, rational functions H=h^n and L=a^N of the Gauss ratios separate u=0,-1, with L pole orders r-1 and q. A separable proper intermediate k(H,L)⊂k(u) would be wildly totally ramified at both points, violating genus-zero Riemann–Hurwitz; hence the Gauss field recovers x,y, so the map is birational. Independent symbolic valuation arithmetic checked seven parameter choices including (q,n,r)=(9,2,5) with degree 26 and (5,2,3) with degree 18. The proof, not the finite scan, establishes all q.
